extracted.intended_audience: students and scholars of philosophy (metaphysics), general readers interested in first principles
extracted.subtask_description: A chapter-length philosophical exposition proposing universal principles (persistence of force, rhythm, and the law of redistribution) that together aim to form a synthetic conception of natural and social change, including evolution (integration) and dissolution (disintegration).

rubrics_metrics.name: Universality of rhythm in motion
rubrics_metrics.description: Rhythm is a necessary characteristic of all motion; given the co-existence of antagonist forces (a postulate of our experience), rhythm is an inevitable corollary of the persistence of force.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explained via examples from tuning-fork vibrations (action↔reaction, momentum↔cohesive tension), orbital motion, tides, commercial cycles, births/deaths, fashions, and other phenomena; rhythm appears at many scales (large waves broken by smaller undulations down to minute ripples), and results whenever accumulated momentum becomes a force at variance with the generating force.

rubrics_metrics.name: Persistence and transformability of force (and relations among forces)
rubrics_metrics.description: Force is persistent and transformable; the persistence of force and the persistence of relations among forces are universal truths co-extensive with various sciences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are not limited to any single science (mechanics, chemistry, astronomy, biology) but illustrated throughout natural and social phenomena; quantitative equivalences among correlates of force (e.g., momentum ↔ tension) are ultimate facts to be recognized.

rubrics_metrics.name: Motion follows the line of least resistance (resultant principle)
rubrics_metrics.description: Motion conforms universally to a law that it follows the line of least resistance, the line of greatest traction, or the resultant of the forces acting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This law applies across scales and kinds of movement — from planetary orbits to organic movements and physical flows — and is presented as an all-pervading principle to be included in any general philosophical account.

rubrics_metrics.name: Analytical truths vs. philosophical synthesis
rubrics_metrics.description: Analytical truths (laws of component factors) are insufficient alone; philosophy must provide a universal synthesis that unites special scientific syntheses into a coherent conception of the whole.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Argument: knowing factors and their laws does not yield the laws of their co-operation; sciences give largely independent syntheses which must be integrated by a higher-level law of composition of phenomena.

rubrics_metrics.name: Law of composition must address matter and motion changes (commencement/cessation/reversal)
rubrics_metrics.description: A satisfactory general formula must specify how both matter and motion change, and must state the conditions under which transformations commence, cease, and reverse.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The law sought should describe rearrangements of component parts and concomitant changes of movement (sensible or insensible) and indicate temporal and conditional boundaries of processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Law of continuous redistribution of matter and motion
rubrics_metrics.description: The general law sought is that of the continuous redistribution of matter and motion: absolute rest and permanence do not exist; every object and the aggregate of objects undergo alteration from instant to instant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consequence: bodies are always gaining or losing motion and changing relations among parts; the law must cover both gradual and rapid changes and be co-extensive with phenomena that can affect consciousness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Completeness of an object's history requires past and future (emergence and disappearance)
rubrics_metrics.description: An entire history of anything must include its appearance from the imperceptible and its disappearance into the imperceptible; accounts that begin or end with a concrete form are incomplete.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Since knowledge is limited to the phenomenal, philosophy must extend scientific genealogies backward and forward to unite past, present, and future into a whole; this motivates seeking a formula unifying concentration and diffusion processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dual processes: integration (concentration) ↔ disintegration (diffusion)
rubrics_metrics.description: Two opposite processes comprehensively characterize change: (1) change from a diffused/imperceptible to a concentrated/perceptible state = integration with concomitant dissipation of motion; (2) change from concentrated/perceptible to diffused/imperceptible = disintegration with concomitant absorption of motion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Axiom: progressing consolidation involves decrease of internal motion; increase of internal motion involves progressing unconsolidation. Constituent aggregation cannot occur without loss of relative motion, and separation cannot occur without gain of relative motion.

rubrics_metrics.name: All change is toward greater concentration or greater diffusion
rubrics_metrics.description: Every change undergone by every sensible existence is a change in one or the other of the two opposite directions (towards integration or towards disintegration).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even apparently quiescent aggregates are slowly gaining or losing substance and motion; thermal, transpositional, and material additions/subtractions all alter average internal distances and therefore advance integration or disintegration. There is no absolutely constant temperature or state: all aggregates progress toward one pole or the other.

rubrics_metrics.name: Concurrent, differential action of integrating and disintegrating processes
rubrics_metrics.description: Both integration and disintegration act simultaneously on aggregates; the net state is a differential result in which one predominates, producing growth, equilibrium cycles, or eventual decay.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: clouds (radiative balance leading to expansion or rain), inorganic objects (passive radiation/absorption), and living organisms (active assimilation and active waste). In living cycles, early integration (growth) predominates, middle cycles show alternation, and late cycles show predominating disintegration (decay). At no moment are assimilation and waste perfectly balanced.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multi-scale oscillations in social and economic phenomena
rubrics_metrics.description: Social changes (commerce, production/consumption, prices, fashion, religion, science) exhibit rhythmic undulations at multiple scales — long epochs, seasonal or yearly cycles, weekly/daily fluctuations, hourly ripples — analogous to physical wave hierarchies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commercial examples: fairs → weekly markets → daily exchanges; prices (consols, wheat) show upward/downward waves of different periods that can be diagrammed like ocean swell with billows and wavelets. Similar multi-scale oscillations occur in births, deaths, disease, crime, and other social statistics.
